Senses.Explanation: Vinaya is the monastic disciplinary code and the learning attached to it. Linji Yixuan asks whether his hearers have ever attended to it, setting the question beside their study of scriptures and treatises. In Muchen Daomin's hall an unnamed monk asks why practitioners do not observe Vinaya; the ensuing exchange tests whether named observance has reached the matter at hand. Yulin Tongxiu calls adaptive discipline ‘Vinaya according to the place.’ Guishan Lingyou's Admonitions names a formal Vinaya seat, while Azi Jinwu and Konggu Daocheng speak of a Vinaya platform and its graded forms. The word therefore marks a concrete disciplinary institution, not a free-floating synonym for virtue, even where masters turn it into a question.
